rationale.coverholder_background:
De La Rue’s purpose is to enable every citizen to participate securely in the global economy. As a trusted partner of governments, central banks and commercial organisations, De La Rue provides products and services that underpin the integrity of trade, personal identity and the movement of goods.
As the world’s largest designer and commercial printer of banknotes, De La Rue designs, manufactures and delivers banknotes, banknote substrates and security features to customers in a world where currency will continue to be a key part of the developing payments eco-system. De La Rue is the only fully integrated supplier of both paper and polymer banknotes, and creates security features that ensure banknotes are protected against counterfeiting

rationale.large_losses:
Clean renewal iro 2023 however 2020 / 2021
The assured has suffered a claim in the expiring period which is currently being adjusted and is expected to be circa GBP202,000 (net of GBP100,000 deductible) from an infestation of a bank note shipment on route to Jamaica. The investigation by Crawfords is still on going and there is some possibility of some subrogation but value and desire to pursue that is still to be advised

September 2010 - A case of Fijian Dollar banknotes was stolen whilst in transit to Fiji from the UK via Singapore. The face value was approx USD500,000. As the customer contract excluded liability for face value, De La Rue’s liability was restricted to reprinting costs + 10% (estimated at the time to be less than £10,000). 
This loss was the subject of a commercial settlement with the Central Bank of Fiji without any insurance claim lodged or paid

rationale.uw_comments:
I am pleased to advise that it is a clean renewal and there are no changes to limits, deductibles, wording or terms and conditions. As I am sure you will recall we are within an LTA, of which this is the first review. A review is not triggered by the loss ratio but it is by the exposure (total value of notes printed/shipped). As you will see the total face value of notes shipped/printed is down circa 67% overall and you will also note there were significantly less movements that were exposed to the layer, flip side though the premises exposures are up, albeit you can argue that is a moot point given the values were already far in excess of the insurance limits. As you will recall the information is always backwards looking so this is the previous 12 months data. You will note from the presentation that the order book for the current year is strong and hence I would assume a return to normal levels next year.

The expiring premium after the LTA discount was GBP495,000 per annum, given the reduced volumes the leader has agreed a renewal premium of GBP445,000 per annum
